Before the iPhone got the app switcher we all know and love, Apple made multitasking available through a sliding drawer that popped up at the bottom of the screen. However, the company experimented with a much more impressive design, showing open apps as on-screen cards. After AppleInsider described an Expose-like interface in early 2010 , a special build of iOS 4 was discovered on an iPhone 4 prototype the very next year. In the decade that followed, nobody had ever showcased the card-like multitasking design - until an emulator developer used AI to bring the scrapped UI back to life.
